openQuestions.question: Which exact wording or tail positions caused the ten live missed claims, and what are the true runtime-specific live cost and warning rates?

resolvedQuestions.question: What drove the reported verdict and what can the available evidence establish?
resolvedQuestions.answer: The paired edge is significant but the 8.18-point gain misses the 10-point margin; aggregate data cannot attribute the ten misses.

resolvedQuestions.question: How can claim accuracy improve while keeping measurement and serving costs bounded?
resolvedQuestions.answer: Use adjudicated misses to build a high-recall candidate layer, never gate on the current regex, and evaluate any cheaper call schedule as a new pre-registered protocol.

resolvedQuestions.question: What would make the labels, corpus and verdict more trustworthy?
resolvedQuestions.answer: Reject duplicate IDs, audit semantic fixture labels, double-label/adjudicate, preserve hashes and model provenance, stratify by runtime and account for session clustering.

resolvedQuestions.question: Where else in .skilled would evidence-backed completion judgment help?
resolvedQuestions.answer: Reuse the evidence contract at explicit closure points: check-completion.sh before done, acceptance-criteria packet closure, and manual-testing success signals; keep the shared advisory core across adapters.

resolvedQuestions.question: What would default-on integration require, cost and risk?
resolvedQuestions.answer: Do not enable Jev now: stop (margin), no named reader. A future phase needs keep, consent, minimal payload, short fail-open async work, kill switch/dedup, and per-runtime call/token/latency/utility measures.

keyFindings.title: Significant paired edge, insufficient margin
keyFindings.summary: Jev gains 9/110=8.18 points; W=13/L=4 gives p_win=0.02452, but the 10-point margin requires at least 11 net rows.

keyFindings.title: Full measurement coverage and unanimous Jev reruns
keyFindings.summary: K=M=110; F=0 means all three Jev calls agreed with the modal output on each row, not that labels are valid.

keyFindings.title: Baseline is lexical and tail-bounded
keyFindings.summary: Ten exact tokens are searched in the last 400 characters; token presence does not encode claim intent.

keyFindings.title: Row-level causes remain unavailable
keyFindings.summary: The real corpus and external report are absent from this packet, preventing per-row attribution or replication.

keyFindings.title: Feature spec cites an obsolete sentinel path
keyFindings.summary: The spec path differs from the scorer import path; behavior evidence comes from the actual runtime/hooks/lib module.

keyFindings.title: Two happy-fixture labels conflict with the scorer question
keyFindings.summary: The failure occurred and outage happened rows are labeled yes though they do not claim completion; this limits synthetic fixture validity, not the absent live labels.

keyFindings.title: Duplicate row or label IDs can silently collapse/overwrite
keyFindings.summary: Rows are accumulated without uniqueness validation then collapsed into a Map; duplicate labels overwrite with Map.set.

keyFindings.title: Missed-claim word census uses substring attribution
keyFindings.summary: firstClaimWord can misattribute substring matches; headline errors remain unaffected.

keyFindings.title: Jev's current measurement costs 331 calls at K=110
keyFindings.summary: One auth test plus 3 uncached calls per label; reduce future evaluation cost only under a newly pre-registered protocol.

keyFindings.title: Hash provenance does not establish representative or valid labels
keyFindings.summary: Report hashes exist but external artifacts, sampling frame, second annotator and per-runtime results are unavailable.

keyFindings.title: The existing completion evidence core spans six advisory runtime adapters
keyFindings.summary: The current regex-based completion hook is enabled by default but only logs advice; this is not a model-backed Jev deployment.

keyFindings.title: Explicit closure gates are the strongest reuse points
keyFindings.summary: check-completion.sh, acceptance-criteria closure and manual-testing validation already have evidence to inspect.

keyFindings.title: The present stop-margin result blocks default-on Jev serving
keyFindings.summary: Feature 026 requires a later phase, keep and named reader; a keep itself does not serve a detector.

keyFindings.title: Future serving needs explicit payload consent and non-blocking evidence delivery
keyFindings.summary: Operator text requires redaction/acceptance; keep fail-open, kill switch/dedup, minimal input and a named reader. Runtime documentation conflicts on Pi visibility: the completion README says the next-turn advisory is model-visible, the injection contract says none enters context, and the Pi adapter calls sendMessage with deliverAs nextTurn.

keyFindings.title: Offline call count is measurable; live volume, price and latency are unknown
keyFindings.summary: 110 labels imply 331 calls under the existing protocol; no supported dollar or monthly live-cost estimate is available.

ruledOutDirections.direction: Attributing all ten missed labels to vocabulary alone
ruledOutDirections.reason: The actual rows and report by-word census are unavailable.

ruledOutDirections.direction: Use the current regex as the sole model-call gate
ruledOutDirections.reason: The reported regex missed all ten labeled claims, so silent positive rows would not be evaluated.

ruledOutDirections.direction: Infer live duplicate rate or annotation validity from synthetic fixtures
ruledOutDirections.reason: The fixture is synthetic and the run-specific corpus and labels are not present.

ruledOutDirections.direction: Default-on Jev judgment in the present completion hook
ruledOutDirections.reason: The measured verdict is stop (margin), and no named live reader is established.

ruledOutDirections.direction: Use the current regex as a model-serving gate
ruledOutDirections.reason: It reportedly misses all ten labeled positives and would hide those cases from the model.
